summary.text: Andrew Sneed is a Huntsville small-business owner and the Democratic nominee for Alabama's 5th Congressional District. A Huntsville native and Boston University graduate, he worked in New York restaurants before returning to Alabama and training as a plumber; he founded a mechanical-contracting company in 2019. He has not previously held office and says he is running on affordability, health care, and government-accountability reforms.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, born and raised in Huntsville, the son of a local attorney and a school teacher/administrator; grew up on the family farm outside town and in Blossomwood.
Graduated from Lee High School in 1998 and earned a BFA from Boston University in 2003.

Spent seven years in New York City after college, working in the restaurant business, before returning to Alabama in 2010. Ballotpedia lists past work as an actor, stuntman, bartender, farmer, and restaurant manager, among others.
At age 32, started over as a $10-an-hour plumber's helper and worked up over about seven years to master plumber and gas fitter, per his campaign website.
Founded his company, Whole Home Solutions, in 2019; his campaign website says it has six work trucks and seven employees (his Ballotpedia survey says a team of eight).

Entered the 2026 Democratic primary for the 5th District; no candidate won a majority on May 19, and he advanced to a June 16 runoff against Candice Dollar Duvieilh, in which the Alabama Democratic Conference endorsed him.

According to his campaign website, he is married and the father of three daughters. He has described a 'Balance / Accountability' pledge that includes term limits and prohibiting stock trading in Congress.
